answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of escrowed tasks whose results are checked against randomly assigned peers; a deposit is slashed when an agent submits fabricated work or colludes with its assigned reviewers. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence: each must lock scarce capital and survive independent audits. A crystal shipment recorded in umber ink might trigger a ripple of cross-checks, but the attacker still pays for every identity that tries to pass.
